entry.title: Aico Grounding: Translating a Natural-Language UI Target Into a Screen Location
entry.summary: Understanding a screenshot is not the same as knowing where to click. That gap is GUI grounding. We've open-sourced Aico Grounding, a local grounding component built to translate a natural-language UI target into a location on the screen. Screenshot + instruction → predicted UI target. [attach annotated screenshot] For a real-device agent, this is one of the critical steps between: seeing the interface The grounding layer runs locally. It identifies interactive elements across the screen, assigns each one a reference, and returns the predicted target location for the agent to act on. The screenshot above shows this running on a real mobile interface — GitHub mobile with the UI in Chinese. The grounding model identifies elements correctly regardless of UI language. Why local grounding matters Cloud-routed grounding adds latency on every action. For a physical device agent that may take dozens of actions in a single task, that adds up fast. Running grounding locally on the Aico hardware keeps the action loop fast and keeps screen content off any external server. What's next More benchmarks and demos coming — including instruction → detected target → actual click end-to-end. GitHub: github.com/AidenAI-IO/aico-grounding

entry.title: 138 new Tesla Superchargers opened in the last 90 days. Here is where.
entry.summary:
I run a free Supercharger directory, and one thing people keep asking me is simple: what opened recently? So I built a page that answers it. As of Nov 18, 2026 it shows: 138 US Supercharger sites opened in the last 90 days (since Aug 20) 1,625 new stalls across those sites Most new sites: California (26), Texas (16), Florida (12), New Jersey (7), Washington (7) 159 more sites are under construction, about 1,980 stalls planned. They are not open yet. The full list, newest first, with city, stall count and max power: https://teslasupercharge.me/new-superchargers Two other pages might help on a road trip: Fastest stalls and biggest stations in the US: https://teslasupercharge.me/fastest-superchargers
A charge-time calculator for the Model 3, Y, S, X and Cybertruck: https://teslasupercharge.me/charge-time
One thing I learned building the calculator: a faster stall does not always mean a faster charge. A Model Y takes up to about 250 kW, so a 325 kW or 500 kW stall gives it the same time as a 250 kW one. Where the stall speed really matters is the older 72 kW and 150 kW sites. How it works, for the technical readers: the whole site is a single Cloudflare Worker that builds every page on request from live station data and caches it for five minutes. There is no database and it runs on the free plan. It is an independent site, not affiliated with Tesla. If a page looks wrong or you want another filter, tell me in the comments.

entry.title: Design Metaprinciples: Less Art, More Engineering
entry.summary:
Design Metaprinciples: Less Art, More Engineering
Software developers love principles, and for a good reason: principles shape how a design is created. They say what to do, what to avoid and, ideally, why. Metaprinciples sit one level up. They shape how the principles themselves are chosen, and they should answer the same "why?" for the whole set. Below are the five metaprinciples that govern the systems I design. To keep them on the ground, I will explain all five with one ordinary thing: a train. Nobody at a railway decides how far apart the rails should be. That question was answered once, the answer is called the gauge, and because of it a car built in one country can run on the lines of another. entry.title: The event loop: the mental model that changes everything
entry.summary: There's a bug that turns up in every Node service sooner or later, and it almost always gets diagnosed wrong. The app serves fine, the logs are clean, the process is alive… and then it stops answering for a few seconds. htop shows one core at 100% and the other eleven watching, bored. It isn't the database. It isn't the network. It's that somebody put CPU work on the only thread allowed to take requests. To understand why that freezes everything, and why setTimeout(fn, 0) doesn't mean "now", you have to open the box. This lesson is the box.
